quandoUsar: Full-page login screen that offers passkey first, with email plus a 6-digit code and three single sign-on providers as alternatives.
Prototypes and demos that need a navigable sign-in flow without a backend: every step is simulated with timers.
Products where signing in and creating an account share the same card: the button at the top switches between “Sign in” and “Sign up” modes.
quandoEvitar: Use `sign-in` when a standalone email-and-code card is enough, without the ring background, header, and page footer.
Use `signup-form` when account creation asks for name, password, and a strength meter.
Use `otp-input` when you already have the flow and only need the code field.

teclado.acao: In the email field or any code cell, submits the form for the current step.
On the code step, move focus between the cells (`otp-input` behavior).
In an empty code cell, clears the previous cell and moves focus back to it.
Moves through the controls of the step; blocked buttons use `aria-disabled` and stay focusable.

acessibilidade: Each step change is announced by a visually hidden `role="status"` region with `aria-live="polite"`; the visible status line in the footer is `aria-hidden`.
Focus follows the flow: it goes to the passkey button, to the email field, to the first code cell, and, on completion, to the welcome heading.
The provider group is a named `role="group"`, each button has its own `aria-label`, and the resend button reports in its `aria-label` how many seconds remain.
movimento: Steps rise into place from a slight blur and, when going back, drop in from above; the card height follows the new content with a spring that does not overshoot, only during the switch.

The background rings drift slightly with the mouse, the outer ones more than the inner ones; on passkey two rings pulse out from the fingerprint, the resend countdown rolls digit by digit, and success draws a circle and a checkmark.
With “reduce motion” on, steps only fade, the height changes instantly, the rings stay still, and the passkey pulse is not rendered.
responsivo: Uses the block's own container queries: below 520 px and 400 px of width, the spacing, the title, and the provider buttons shrink.
Fills the container width with a minimum height of 640 px; `fullScreen` switches to `min-height: 100dvh` and removes the border and radius.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` measures the card to animate its height, and the resend countdown uses a 1 s timer only on the code step; all timers are cleared on unmount.
notasIA: Nothing is actually authenticated: `startPasskey`, `submitEmail`, `verify`, and `signInWith` use `setTimeout`, and `onSignIn(email, method, mode)` only signals that the simulation finished; replace these functions with the real calls.
Props: `fullScreen` to fill the page, `demoCode` (the accepted code, default `482913`), `demoEmail` (the account returned by passkey and providers), `termsHref`, and `privacyHref`.
Depends on `button`, `input`, and `otp-input`; the “ryan-ui” brand and all texts are hardcoded in English in the file, with no props to translate them.

quandoUsar: Social-proof strip on a landing page: customers, integrations, or compatible tools passing in a continuous line.
When there are enough brands for one copy of the list to be wider than the section and none of them needs emphasis or a link.
quandoEvitar: Use `marquee` when the scrolling content is not a list of brands or when you need to control speed, direction, or vertical scrolling.
With few brands, prefer a static grid: if one copy of the list is narrower than the section, the loop does not close and a gap appears at the end.
If each logo needs to be a link or open a customer case, this block does not fit: items are only a symbol and a name, with no interaction.

teclado.acao: On the “Pause” or “Play” button, pause or resume the strip's motion.

acessibilidade: The strip is a named `role="region"`, the duplicated copy of the list is `aria-hidden`, and the symbols are decorative: each brand's name is real text.
The pause button has an `aria-label` that switches between pause and resume, and an `aria-live="polite"` region announces “Motion paused”.
The accessible names of the region and the button are hardcoded in English in the file (“Illustrative tool logos”, “Pause logo motion”); adjust them when you swap the brands.
movimento: The strip slides left in a continuous 39 s loop with a linear CSS animation; hovering over it or pressing the button freezes the motion where it is.
With “reduce motion” on, the animation is removed, the brands become a centered list that wraps onto lines, the duplicated copy disappears, and the pause button is hidden.
responsivo: A container query on the section (up to 639 px) stacks the title and description, reduces the type size, and brings the brands closer together.
desempenho: The motion is a single CSS `transform` animation on the strip, with no per-frame JavaScript; each symbol is painted as a CSS mask from the SVG URL, so use small files.
notasIA: Pass `brands` with `name` and `icon` (URL of a monochrome SVG, used as a mask); `color` paints the symbol in the `color` tone and `colorIcon` replaces the mask with a color image.
The default brands are abstract example shapes, not real logos; the loop duration is fixed at 39 s, so longer lists move faster.
`tone="mono"` draws everything in the text color; there is no `className` prop, and the block depends on `button`.

quandoUsar: Search in an app's top bar where space is tight: at rest it is just a 44 px icon and opens on click or with the `/` key.
Quick navigation through a local list of pages, people, and actions, grouped by type and limited to a few results (`limit`, default 6).
quandoEvitar: Use `command-palette` when search is the main command surface, with per-item shortcuts, and not a field inside the bar.
Use `expanding-search` when you need recent suggestions before typing or a custom accessible name for the field; here the labels are hardcoded in English.
Use `search-field` when the field is always visible and the results appear elsewhere on the screen.

teclado.acao: Opens the search from anywhere on the page, as long as focus is not in a text field; the key comes from `shortcut`.
Move the highlight through the results list, wrapping around at the ends.
Selects the highlighted result, calls `onSelect`, closes the search, and returns focus to the icon.
First clears the text; with an empty field, closes the search and returns focus to the icon.
Closes the search and clears the text, without preventing focus from moving on.

acessibilidade: The field is a `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-activedescendant`; results are `role="option"` inside a `listbox`, in groups named by their headings.
Focus stays on the field while the highlight moves through the options; when closed, the search sets the field to `disabled` and the panel to `inert`, and the no-results state uses `role="status"`.
The accessible names (“Search”, “Results”, “Clear search”) and the “Suggested …” headings are hardcoded in English in the file.
movimento: The icon stretches into the field with a spring that does not overshoot, and only then does the results panel grow downward; on close, the panel folds first and the field shrinks afterward.
A single highlight slides between rows following the arrows or the pointer, and results enter rising 8 px and reposition when the list filters.
With “reduce motion” on, width, height, highlight, and rows change instantly.
responsivo: The open width is the smaller of `width` (default 440 px) and the measured space of the anchor, so the field never exceeds the container.
Below 36rem of viewport, the keyboard hints line in the panel footer is hidden.
desempenho: Filtering is local and synchronous over `items` on every keystroke, with no loading state: it suits in-memory lists, not remote search.
Uses two `ResizeObserver`s (anchor and panel) and `document` listeners only while needed: `keydown` for the shortcut when closed and `pointerdown` when open.
notasIA: Import the named component `MorphingSearch`; the file's default export is `MorphingSearchPreview`, the demo with a fictional app around it.

The anchor takes 100% of the parent's width and reserves only 44 px of height: the field grows up to `width` from the `align` edge and floats over the content, so the parent must provide that space and must not clip with `overflow: hidden`.
Only `title` and `keywords` are searched (`subtitle` is not); control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`, `query` and `onQueryChange`, and pass `shortcut=""` to turn off the global key.

quandoUsar: Section switching inside a card or page where the switch itself deserves attention: the active pill travels, stretching toward the new tab.
A few tabs with short labels whose panels have different heights: the content area animates the height from one panel to the other.
quandoEvitar: Use `tabs` when you need to compose triggers and panels freely or keep panels mounted; here only the active panel exists in the DOM.
Use `segmented-control` when the choice only changes a mode or filter and there is no associated panel.
Use `expandable-tabs` when the tabs are icons and the space only fits the label of the active tab.

teclado.acao: Select the next or previous tab, wrapping around at the ends and skipping disabled ones; selection follows focus.
Select the first or last enabled tab.
Enters the list at the active tab and then moves to the panel, which is focusable.

acessibilidade: Follows the tabs pattern: `role="tablist"` with `aria-label` coming from `label`, tabs with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and a `role="tabpanel"` panel linked by `aria-labelledby`.
Uses roving tabindex (only the active tab is in the Tab order), and the colored copy of the row that forms the pill is `aria-hidden`.
The default `label` is “Sections”, in English; pass the real name of the tab set.
movimento: The pill is a clip (`clip-path`) of a copy of the row in the highlight color: the leading edge arrives first with a fast spring and the trailing edge follows with a slower one, which stretches the pill.

While stretched it thins (up to 5 px less at top and bottom) and gets squarer corners, and returns to the pill shape on arrival; the panel exits and enters sliding 36 px in the direction of travel, with the height on a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the pill jumps to the new tab and the panel and height change instantly.
responsivo: If the row of tabs is wider than the available space, it scrolls horizontally with the scrollbar hidden; below 26rem of viewport the tabs' side padding shrinks.
desempenho: The pill animates only `clip-path` from two motion values, with no per-frame layout; labels and icons are rendered twice because of the colored copy.
notasIA: Import the named component `MorphingTabs`; the file's default export is the preview with an example card.
The API is an array: `tabs` with `id`, `label`, `icon`, `content`, and `disabled`; control it with `value` and `onValueChange` or use `defaultValue`.
Because only the active panel stays mounted, local state inside `content` is lost when switching tabs; and the list's 4 px inset in the CSS must match the component's `INSET` constant.

quandoUsar: Newsletter signup section on a landing page or blog where showing past issues helps people decide.
Standalone signup card (`variant="card"`), for example at the end of an article.
Email-only form with validation and submit states, without the stack: pass `publication={null}` and `readers={null}`.
quandoEvitar: Use `site-footer` when the signup is just a field inside the footer; its columns variant already includes a newsletter form.
Use `contact-section` when the person needs to write a message, and `signup-form` when the goal is to create an account with a password.
Without real issues to show, the stack becomes decoration with example data; in that case hide it instead of inventing content.

teclado.acao: In the email field, submits the form; with an invalid address, focus returns to the field.

acessibilidade: The field has a visually hidden `<label>` (“Email address”), `aria-invalid` when the address is invalid, and `aria-describedby` pointing to the message line.
The message line sits in an `aria-live="polite"` region and becomes `role="alert"` on error; on completion, focus goes to “Use a different email” and, on reset, returns to the field.
Only the front issue of the stack is exposed to the screen reader, with an `aria-label`; the ones behind are `aria-hidden` and the reader photos have empty `alt`.
movimento: On subscribe, the next issue rises from below, addressed to the typed email, and lands at the front of the stack; the previous ones step back one level on a spring that does not overshoot and the oldest leaves.
The button label swaps in place between submit, submitting, and subscribed (with a drawn checkmark), the reader count goes up by one, and an error shakes the field sideways once.
With “reduce motion” on, issues take their place instantly and only fade, there is no shake or checkmark drawing, and the submit indicator spins more slowly.
responsivo: The block's container queries: up to 860 px the `inline` variant stacks the text and the stack; up to 520 px and 400 px the spacing shrinks and the reading minutes disappear.
The form has its own container: up to 300 px, the field and button separate and stack at full width; the message line reserves the height of the longest sentence, so nothing below moves.
desempenho: Thumbnails and faces go through `RyanImage`, which loads on demand by default; an invisible copy of the next issue stays in the DOM only to reserve the stack's height.
notasIA: Import the named component `NewsletterSignup`; the default export is `NewsletterSignupBlock`, the preview with layout switching and a switch that simulates failure.
Pass `onSubscribe(email)` returning a Promise: rejecting shows the error and keeps the email, resolving shows success; without this prop the block just waits 1.1 s and pretends it worked.

`publication` (name, `upcoming`, and `recent`) and `readers` come with example data from `newsletter-signup-data.ts`; replace them with your own or pass `null`, and note that the validation messages are hardcoded in English.

quandoUsar: 404 page of a site or app that has a few known destinations to suggest and, preferably, a search to send the query to.
Products where an error page can have a light tone: the illustration has a zero with a face that follows the mouse and jumps when clicked.
quandoEvitar: Use `empty-state` when the page exists but a list or search has nothing to show.
Use `alert` for a recoverable error inside a screen that is still useful.
For a 500 error or maintenance the art does not fit: the two fours and the zero are drawn in the file's SVG.

teclado.acao: In the search field, submits the form and calls `onSearch` with the text trimmed at both ends.

acessibilidade: The section is named by the title's `<h1>`, and the illustration is a `role="img"` with an English `aria-label`, hardcoded in the file.
The search is a `role="search"` form whose field uses `searchPlaceholder` as its `aria-label`; the “N of M pages match” line is `aria-live="polite"` and announces the filter result.
The zero's jump on click has no keyboard equivalent or button role: it is decoration and carries no information.
movimento: The pieces land one after another with a slightly bouncy spring: the fours and the zero fall from above and the smaller shapes appear growing.
At rest, CSS animations make the zero float and blink, the second four sway, and the shapes drift and rotate; with a mouse, the eyes follow the pointer and the layers shift at different depths.
With “reduce motion” on, the illustration appears still, with no loops, no pointer following, and no jump, and the filtered links change instantly.
responsivo: The block is a centered column up to 36rem; below 30rem of viewport the link grid goes from two columns to one and the spacing shrinks.
notasIA: Import the named component `NotFound`; the default export is `NotFoundPreview`, which blocks link navigation for the demo.
Pass your site's `links` (each `href` is used as a key and must be unique) and `onSearch` to carry the query to your search; without `onSearch`, submitting the form does nothing.
For client-side routing, use `onNavigate(link, event)` and call `event.preventDefault()`; the block renders an `<h1>`, so it should be the page's main content.

quandoUsar: Notification inbox behind a bell in an app header, with read and unread state and a count on the badge.
When the person needs to triage: open a notification's detail, mark it as read, dismiss it, mark all as read, or clear the read ones.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast` or `toast-stack` for the immediate feedback of an action the person just took.
Use `notification-stack` when notifications stay visible on the page as a stack of cards dismissed one by one, with no read state.
Use `timeline` for a full-page activity history, grouped by day.

teclado.acao: On the bell, open or close the panel; on a row, show or hide the detail with its actions.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the bell.
Move through the panel's controls: close, the “All” and “Unread” filters, rows, and actions.

acessibilidade: It is a Radix popover: the bell receives `aria-expanded` from the primitive and an `aria-label` with `label` plus the unread count; the panel carries an `aria-label` and the summary is `aria-live="polite"`.
Each row is a button with `aria-expanded` and a name that combines the title, the unread state, and the show-or-hide-details action; the filters use `aria-pressed`.
Focus is repositioned after each action: on dismiss it goes to the neighboring row, and after bulk actions it goes to the filter buttons.
movimento: The panel grows from the bell, which tilts 12° while open; rows enter in a 35 ms cascade and collapse their own height on a spring when leaving, in sequence on bulk actions.

The counts roll like an odometer (the larger number rises from below, the smaller one descends from above), the filter highlight slides between “All” and “Unread”, and the mark-as-read button animates its width when its label changes.
With “reduce motion” on, the CSS animations are removed and changes become a short fade or happen instantly.
responsivo: The panel has width `min(424px, 100vw - 24px)` and maximum height `min(590px, 100vh - 24px)`; the list scrolls inside, with the scrollbar hidden.
Up to 380 px of viewport the spacing shrinks and “Mark all read” loses its text, leaving only the icon.
desempenho: All notifications are rendered at once, each row with a height animation and no virtualization; keep the list in the tens.
notasIA: `notifications` is only the initial state (it goes into a `useState`): later changes to the prop are ignored, so to inject new notifications remount with a different `key`.
Persist with `onReadChange(notification, read)` and `onDismiss(notification)`, called once per item also on bulk actions; `time` is ready-made text, the component does not format dates.
Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/notification-center/notification-center` (it does not live in `blocks/`); it already draws the bell, depends on `avatar`, and accepts `open` with `onOpenChange`.

quandoUsar: A handful of pending notifications on a panel or dashboard, stacked to take little space and opened into a list when the person gets close.
Notifications that resolve by dismissing: drag the card sideways, a close button, or the `Delete` key.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast-stack` for transient results that appear at the screen edge and disappear on their own.
Use `notification-center` when you need read and unread state, a filter, and bulk actions behind a bell.
Use `swipe-actions` when the sideways gesture should reveal actions on a list row, and not remove the item.

teclado.acao: When entering the stack by keyboard it opens into a list; each card has one stop, on the dismiss button.
Dismiss the focused card and move focus to the next card, or to the “Bring them back” button when the stack empties.
Activate the focused button: dismiss a card, pin the list open (“Show all”), or clear everything (“Clear all”).

acessibilidade: With the stack closed, the cards behind are `aria-hidden` and out of the Tab order; the “Show all” button pins the list open and exposes `aria-expanded`.
A hidden `role="status"` announces how many notifications remain, each close button has an `aria-label` with the card's title, and the unread dot carries the text “Unread” for screen readers.
Dragging is not the only path: the close button and `Delete` do the same, and on touch screens a tap on the stack opens it.
movimento: Closed, each card behind shows 10 px and shrinks 5%; with the mouse over it, keyboard focus, or a pinned list, the cards drop into a list on a spring and the container height follows.
A dismissed card slides toward the drag side and disappears, and the others move up to close the line on a spring; dragging past 110 px or releasing above 650 px/s confirms the exit.
With “reduce motion” on, dragging is turned off, cards only fade out when leaving, and positions change instantly.
responsivo: The width is `min(25rem, 100%)` and each card's text is clipped to two lines, which keeps all of them the same height.
The open list grows downward in the page flow and pushes what comes after; `touch-action: pan-y` lets vertical scrolling through while the sideways drag dismisses.
desempenho: All notifications stay mounted, even those that do not show in the stack, each with its own `ResizeObserver` and drag; the block was designed for few items, not hundreds.
notasIA: Import the named component `NotificationStack`; the default export is the preview with example notifications.
Control it with `notifications` and `onNotificationsChange` (list from newest to oldest) or use `defaultNotifications`; `onDismiss(id)` fires per card, including for each one in “Clear all”.
In controlled mode also pass `defaultNotifications`: the empty state's “Bring them back” button returns that list and, without it, hands the example notifications to your `onNotificationsChange`.

quandoUsar: Fixed-length verification code, sent by email or SMS or generated by an authenticator app, typed cell by cell.
When pasting the whole code needs to work: the pasted text is distributed across the cells starting from the focused one.
quandoEvitar: Use `sign-in` when you want the whole email-and-code flow already assembled, with resend and account state.
Use `input` for variable-length codes or codes with separators, such as coupons and recovery keys.
Use `password-field` for secrets that should not appear on screen; here the characters are visible.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next cell.
In an empty cell, clears the previous cell and moves focus to it.
Clears the character in the focused cell.
Pastes the code starting from the focused cell; in numeric mode, anything that is not a digit is discarded.
Go through each cell: all of them are independent fields in the focus order.

acessibilidade: The cells form a `role="group"` with an `aria-label` coming from `label`, and each field identifies itself as “digit N of M”, in English hardcoded in the file.
`description` and `error` are linked to all cells by `aria-describedby`; with an error, the cells receive `aria-invalid` and the message is a `role="alert"`.
The first cell uses `autoComplete="one-time-code"`; in forced colors the animated ring disappears and the native focus outline returns.
movimento: Each digit rises into the cell from a slight blur; when pasting, the digits arrive in a wave from left to right.
A single focus ring slides between cells with a short spring, and a new error shakes the row sideways once, with the message opening its own height.
With “reduce motion” on, digits only fade, the ring jumps between cells, there is no shake, and messages appear without animation.
responsivo: The cells are 42 × 48 px and shrink in width when the row does not fit; up to 360 px of viewport the gap between them drops to 6 px and the height to 44 px.
notasIA: It is controlled only: without `value` and `onChange` the typed digits do not appear; `onChange` returns the compact string, so check `value.length === length` to validate or submit.
`label` is required; `length` is 6 by default, `inputMode="text"` accepts letters, and passing a new `error` triggers the shake.

Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/otp-input/otp-input` (it does not live in `blocks/`); there is no `onComplete`, and `sign-in` and `login-centered` show how to submit when the last cell is completed.

quandoUsar: Toolbar whose width changes (resizable panels, narrow columns, small screens) and that has more actions than fit.
When all actions must stay reachable: the ones that do not fit go into the “more” menu, starting with the last ones in the list.
quandoEvitar: Use `button-group` when there are a few related actions that always fit.
Use `dropdown-menu` when secondary actions can live in a menu from the start.
Use `toggle-group` for formatting toggles that always fit and do not need a menu.

teclado.acao: Move focus between the visible actions and the “more” button, wrapping around at the ends and skipping disabled ones.
Move focus to the first or last stop of the bar.
The bar has a single Tab stop; the arrow keys do the rest.
Activate the focused action or open the “more” menu.
In the “more” menu, move between items; `↓` on the button also opens the menu.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the “more” button.

acessibilidade: The bar is a `role="toolbar"` with an `aria-label` coming from `label` and roving tabindex; actions with `pressed` expose `aria-pressed`.
The “more” button receives `moreLabel` with the count in the `aria-label`, and in the menu an active action gets a dot with the text “On” for screen readers.
The measuring row, with copies of all the actions, is `aria-hidden` and `inert`.
movimento: Actions that stop fitting shrink to 80% and fade, and the ones that return do the reverse; the “more” button slides to its new position on a layout spring.
The number on the “more” button rolls vertically when the count changes, and the menu opens with the items in a 28 ms cascade.
With “reduce motion” on, entries, exits, and shifts happen instantly and the menu animations are removed.
responsivo: The width that counts is the component's own, which takes 100% of its parent: it measures all the actions in a hidden row and shows as many as fit, never wrapping to a new line.
When no action fits, only the “more” button remains, with all of them inside the menu.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` watches the root and the measuring row and recomputes on every change of width, label, or font; each action is rendered twice because of that copy.
notasIA: Import the named component `OverflowActions`; the default export is the preview of an editor with a resize handle.
Order `actions` by priority, because the last ones go to the menu first, and give the container a real width (in flex, `min-width: 0`).
`pressed` is controlled by you: keep the state and toggle it in `onSelect` or `onAction(id)`; `onOverflowChange(ids)` reports which actions are in the menu.

quandoUsar: Starting point for a project page header in an app: breadcrumb, title with status, members, actions, and section tabs with counts.
Long screens where the title should get out of the way on scroll without disappearing: the header folds into a compact bar that takes you back to the top.
quandoEvitar: Use `site-header` for a site's top navigation; this block is the header of a page inside the product.
Use `tabs` or `breadcrumb` when you only need the section switch or only the breadcrumb, not the whole set.
If the page scrolls the window, the fold does not happen: it reads the scroll of the block's inner body, which has a fixed height of 640 px.

teclado.acao: In the sections row, move focus to the neighboring tab and select it right away, wrapping around at the ends (Radix tabs).
Select the first or last section.
From the active tab, moves on to the section panel, which is focusable.
On the three-dot button, open the actions menu (Radix).
In the actions menu, move between items and wrap around at the ends.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the three-dot button.

acessibilidade: The breadcrumb sits in a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with `aria-current="page"`; when folded it becomes `inert` and a button with the title takes over, scrolling to the top and moving focus to the `<h2>`.
The results of the actions (follow, share, create or complete an issue, copy the link) are announced by a `role="status"` region, and the visual notice is `aria-hidden`.
When an issue is completed, focus moves to the next issue's button or to the panel when the list empties; below 460 px “New issue” becomes icon-only and keeps its `aria-label`.
movimento: Scrolling the body past 16 px folds the header: the intro collapses its height on a spring that does not overshoot, the title shrinks and blurs, and the breadcrumb gives way to the compact title, which only reopens at 4 px from the top.
The active tab's underline slides between tabs, the counts roll, the panel enters sliding 12 px in the direction of the chosen tab, and issue rows open and close their own height.
With “reduce motion” on, the fold, panels, and rows change instantly or only fade, the underline jumps, and the CSS transitions are removed.
responsivo: When the bar gets narrow, “Follow” and “Share update” collapse into the three-dot menu (width on a spring) and only return with some slack, without flickering at the threshold.

The frame's container queries: up to 559 px the first breadcrumb level disappears, the tabs row scrolls sideways with a faded edge, and the rows rearrange; on screens up to 560 px the frame takes almost the full height.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` on the bar alone decides when to collapse the actions, and the timers for the simulated actions and the 3.2 s notice are cleared on unmount.
notasIA: `PageHeader` takes no props: project, breadcrumb, people, issues, updates, and files are constants in the file and the actions are simulated, so copy the installed file and replace the data and handlers with your own.
The fold depends on the inner body with its own scroll (`.scroller`) inside a fixed-height frame; with `auto` height the body does not scroll and the header never folds.
Needs `animated-counter`, `avatar`, `avatar-group`, `badge`, `button`, and `progress`, plus the Radix tabs and menu; the example photos come from `@/lib/media`.

quandoUsar: Pricing section that compares two plans row by row, with a switch between monthly and annual billing and a filter to show only the differences.
Starting point for editing: plans, prices, and features are constants at the top of the file, ready to be replaced with your own.
quandoEvitar: Use `comparison-table` to compare your product with competitors, with a sticky header and a highlighted column.
Use `billing-toggle` when you only need the period switch with rolling prices, in plan cards.
For three or more plans the block does not work as is: the grid and the `Feature` type have exactly two columns, Team and Studio.

teclado.acao: In the period selector, switch between monthly and annual and move focus along (`segmented-control`).
On the “Show differences only” switch, turn the filter on or off; on a plan button, select or clear the selection.

acessibilidade: The matrix uses ARIA table roles (`table`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `cell`), and each value carries the plan name in hidden text, so it makes sense read on its own.
The plan buttons expose `aria-pressed` and a `role="status"` region announces the chosen plan; each plan's price sits in an `aria-live="polite"` region with `aria-atomic`.
The filter is the `switch` labeled “Show differences only” and the period is the `segmented-control` named “Billing period”.
movimento: Switching the period makes each price count up to the new value in 0.24 s, and the “N of 8 features” count follows the filter.

Turning on the filter collapses the height of the identical feature rows on a spring that does not overshoot and reopens them with a fade; choosing a plan tints the column and a 2 px rail slides to it.
With “reduce motion” on, the numbers change instantly, rows enter and leave without animation, and the rail jumps.
responsivo: The layout follows the block's width, measured by a `ResizeObserver`: up to 720 px the intro stacks and the margins shrink; up to 540 px the feature name moves above the two values and the “What changes” column disappears.
notasIA: `PlanComparison` takes no props: edit `features` (with `shared: true` on what the filter hides) and `pricing` at the top of the file, and the hardcoded texts in the JSX.
The “Select …” buttons only mark the plan with `aria-pressed`, with no callback; hook up your checkout by replacing their `onClick`.
The “Included” and “Not included” values are compared as exact text to get the checkmark and the muted tone; the block depends on `button`, `segmented-control`, and `switch`.

quandoUsar: Yes-or-no market with play money, in demos, educational content, or games: price of each outcome, probability history, and a ticket with an estimated return.
When the person needs to read the history point by point, with a pointer or keyboard, and see the return update while typing the amount.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when you only need to show the historical series, or several series, without the purchase ticket.
Use `token-swap` to exchange one asset for another with rate and fee.
For real money the block is not enough: balance and position live only in local state and a rejected order returns to the start with no error message.

teclado.acao: On the focused chart, read the previous or next point of the series; the value read is announced.
On the chart, jump to the first or last point of the period.
In the period and outcome selectors (Yes and No), choose the neighboring option, move focus along, and wrap around at the ends.
Each selector is a single stop, on the chosen option, and the chart is another stop.

acessibilidade: The chart is a focusable `role="group"` whose `aria-label` gives the current probability and explains the arrow keys; the point read is announced by an `aria-live="polite"` region and the SVG is `aria-hidden`.
Period and outcome are `role="radiogroup"` with `role="radio"` buttons, `aria-checked`, and roving tabindex.

The amount field has a label, `aria-invalid` above the balance, and `aria-describedby` for the estimate; the buy button receives `aria-busy` while submitting and the position line is `aria-live="polite"`.
movimento: The line draws itself in 1.1 s the first time; switching period or outcome transforms the path on a spring that does not overshoot and the end marker slides to the new point, pulsing at rest.
Probability, prices, shares, return, and balance count up to each new value in 0.48 s, the selection pills slide, and the button label goes through “Placing order” and “Order placed”.
With “reduce motion” on, the numbers change instantly, the line appears without drawing or transformation, pills and marker jump, and the pulse and the submit indicator stop.
responsivo: The card goes up to 27rem; the chart has a fixed height of 136 px and a width measured by a `ResizeObserver`, and up to 26rem of viewport the inner padding shrinks.
notasIA: Import the named component `PredictionMarket` (the default export is the preview with example data) and control the outcome with `side` and `onSideChange` or use `defaultSide`.
In `ranges`, every period needs the same number of `points` (probability of “Yes”, from 0 to 1) and one `labels` item per point; the last point of the active period is the current price.
`onPlaceOrder(order)` receives `side`, `amount`, `price`, and `shares`: return a Promise to hold “Placing order” and show your own error if it rejects; `balance` is only the starting balance.

quandoUsar: Grid or shelf of projects in portfolios, dashboards, and file home screens, where peeking at the first documents on hover gives context.
To show at a glance the kind of content in a folder (text, chart, or image) before opening it.
quandoEvitar: Use `file-tree` to actually navigate files and subfolders, with selection and keyboard.
Use `card-folder` when the content is a set of cards with tabs to read one at a time.
If opening the folder should list or open files, the block alone is not enough: when open, it only draws three sheets, with no links.

teclado.acao: Open or close the folder, spreading out or gathering the sheets.
With focus coming from the keyboard, the folder opens slightly as on mouse hover.

acessibilidade: The whole folder is a native `<button>` with `aria-expanded`; the drawing (tab, sheets, and counter) is `aria-hidden`, so the accessible name comes from the name and the line below it.
When open, the line below swaps the description for the names of the first three sheets plus “and N more”, hardcoded in English, and that is what the screen reader then announces.
The sheet images have empty `alt`, because they are decorative.
movimento: With the mouse over it or keyboard focus, the tab tilts back 24° in 3D and the sheets peek out; on click, the tab opens to 42° and the sheets rise in a fan on a slightly bouncy spring, 45 ms one after another.
The tab uses a heavier spring, with practically no bounce; on close, the sheets return in reverse order and the line under the name swaps with a short slide.
With “reduce motion” on, the tab does not rotate, the sheets jump into place, and the line only fades.
responsivo: Everything scales from `--folder-size` (default 13rem), set on the folder or a parent; the folder reserves space above itself for the sheets to rise, but when open they extend slightly past the sides.
notasIA: Import the named component `ProjectFolder`; the default export is a shelf of three folders where opening one closes the others, built with `open` and `onOpenChange`.
`files` draws only the first three sheets (`kind` `text`, `chart`, or `image`, with `image` for the URL) and counts the rest; to show the real content, react to `onOpenChange`.
Leave side space between neighboring folders for the open fan; `tone="accent"` paints the folder in the accent color and the sheets' paper stays light in both themes.

quandoUsar: Standalone sign-in card on your own page, with email plus a 6-digit code as the main path and passkey and three single sign-on providers as alternatives.
Prototypes that need a navigable sign-in flow without a backend: submit, verification, and providers are simulated with timers.
When it is worth fixing common domain mistakes in the email: “gmial.com” becomes the suggestion “gmail.com”, applied with one click.
quandoEvitar: Use `login-centered` when the login takes the full screen, passkey should come first, or the same card needs to switch to account creation.
Use `signup-form` to create an account with name, password, and terms acceptance.
Use `otp-input` when you already have the flow and only need the code field.

teclado.acao: In the email field, moves on to the code; in a code cell, submits the verification, which also fires on its own when all 6 cells are filled.
On the code step, move focus between the cells (`otp-input` behavior).
In an empty code cell, clears the previous one and moves focus back to it.
Moves through the controls of the step; the resend button stays focusable during the countdown, with `aria-disabled`.

acessibilidade: Each step change is announced by a hidden `role="status"` region with `aria-live="polite"`; the visible status line in the footer is `aria-hidden`.
Focus follows the flow: first code cell, welcome heading on completion, and the email field, with its text selected, when changing email or leaving.
The providers form a named `role="group"` with an `aria-label` per button, the resend says in its `aria-label` how many seconds remain, and the domain suggestion is a “Use …” button.
movimento: Steps cross sideways coming out of a slight blur, returning from the opposite side, and the card height follows the new step on a spring that does not overshoot only during the switch.
On completion via the code, the small avatar grows into the large one (shared layout), a ring draws around it, a checkmark badge appears, and the title, details, and button rise in sequence.
With “reduce motion” on, steps only fade, the height changes instantly, and the avatar, ring, and badge appear without animation.
responsivo: The card uses `min(100%, 432px)`; a container query up to 380 px tightens margins, title, and provider buttons, and up to 480 px of viewport the radius shrinks.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` measures the content to animate the height and the resend countdown uses a 1 s timer only on the code step; timers are cleared on unmount.
notasIA: Nothing is actually authenticated: `submitEmail`, `verify`, and `signInWith` use `setTimeout` and `onSignIn(account, method)` only signals the end of the simulation; replace these functions with the real calls.
There are only two props, `demoCode` (default `123456`, shown as a hint in the code field) and `onSignIn`; remove the hint in production and note that the texts are hardcoded in English.
Depends on `avatar`, `button`, `input`, and `otp-input`; the footer's “Sign up” only changes the status line, so hook it up to your signup route, for example with `signup-form`.

quandoUsar: Account-creation page or card with single sign-on (Google, Apple, GitHub) and, below it, name, work email, and a password with a strength meter.
Flows where the error should appear on the right field: messages show up when leaving a filled field or on submit, and focus goes to the first invalid one.
When creation needs to end in a clear completion state, showing the method used and the email preference, without changing pages.
quandoEvitar: Use `sign-in` or `login-centered` for people who already have an account.
Use `newsletter-signup` when you only need to collect an email.
Use `password-strength` when you want only the strength meter inside a form of your own.

teclado.acao: In any field, submits the form; with an error, focus goes to the first invalid field.
On the “Email me product updates” box, checks or unchecks it (Radix checkbox).

acessibilidade: The fields come from `input` and `password-field`, with a visible label and an error message linked to each one; on submit with an error, focus goes to the first invalid field.
The strength line is linked to the password by `aria-describedby` and becomes `role="alert"` on error; the colored meter is `aria-hidden`, so the level arrives in words, from “Weak” to “Strong”.
The submit error, yours (`serverError`) or thrown by `onSubmit`, appears in `role="alert"`; steps are announced by `role="status"` and the welcome heading receives focus on completion.
movimento: Steps cross sideways coming out of a slight blur, the card height follows on a spring that does not overshoot only during the switch, and completion draws a circle and then a checkmark.
The strength text swaps in place rising from a slight blur while the meter lights up bar by bar, with a color per level, and the submit error line opens its own height on a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, steps only fade, the height and lines change instantly, the checkmark appears already drawn, and the meter changes color without a transition.
responsivo: The card uses `min(100%, 432px)`; a container query up to 380 px tightens margins, title, provider buttons, and meter bars, and up to 480 px of viewport the radius shrinks.
notasIA: `onSubmit(details)` receives `name`, `email`, `password`, and `productUpdates`; throw an `Error` to show its message, and note that completion waits at least 700 ms even with a fast response.
`serverError` shows an error from your API above the button; `onProvider(provider)` is called on click, but the block simulates the redirect and completes in 900 ms with example data.
The rules are fixed (name with 2 or more characters, complete email, password with 8 or more) and the messages are in English; “Terms”, “Privacy policy”, and “Sign in” only change the status line.

quandoUsar: Footer for a product or documentation site with link columns, newsletter signup, legal links, social networks, and a system status link.
Discreet two-line footer (`variant="minimal"`) for pages where columns would be excessive.
Closing a ryan-ui landing page with the large gradient brand (`variant="logo"`).
quandoEvitar: Use `newsletter-signup` when the signup is the section's main call, with the issue stack and the reader count.
Use `cta-section` to close the page with a call to action instead of navigation.
The `variant="logo"` variant only works for the ryan-ui brand: the large arc is drawn in the file and `brand.mark` only changes the small icon.

teclado.acao: In the newsletter field, submits the signup; if empty or invalid, the error appears right there.

acessibilidade: The columns sit in a `<nav aria-label="Footer">` with each heading in an `<h2>`, the legal and social lists have an `aria-label`, and links without `href` become a `<button>`.
The newsletter field has a hidden label, `aria-invalid`, and `aria-describedby` for the message line, which is `aria-live="polite"` and becomes `role="alert"` on error.
`external` links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, but the notice is only the `aria-hidden` arrow; if it matters, include “new tab” in the `label`.
movimento: In the `logo` variant, the large arc rises 40 px and appears in 0.9 s the first time 30% of it enters the screen, cut off by the bottom edge and fading into the brand gradient.
The newsletter line swaps in place between hint, error, and confirmation, rising from a slight blur, and the arrow on external links shifts on hover.
With “reduce motion” on, the arc appears already drawn, messages change instantly, and the link and field transitions are removed.
responsivo: The footer's container queries: up to 760 px the brand and newsletter stack above the columns; up to 520 px the columns become two, the newsletter takes the full width, and the bottom line stacks.
notasIA: Import the named component `SiteFooter`; the default export is `SiteFooterBlock`, the preview with layout switching, and all props have ryan-ui example values for you to replace.
Pass `columns`, `legal`, and `socials` with `href`, because without it the links become buttons that only call `onNavigate`; `newsletter={null}` and `status={null}` hide those parts.
`newsletter.onSubscribe(email)` can return a Promise: rejecting shows the error and resolving shows “Subscribed”; without the function, the block waits 0.9 s and pretends success.

quandoUsar: Top navigation for a product or documentation site: brand, a few sections, “Sign in,” and a primary action, fixed at the top and opaque on scroll.
Sections with many destinations that call for mega menu panels with a description per link and a featured card (`variant="mega"`).
Sites that need to work on mobile: below 760 px of header width, the links fold into a menu sheet.
quandoEvitar: Use `page-header` for the header of a page inside the app, with project title, tabs, and actions.
Use `animated-sidebar` when the app's navigation is a side menu with groups and many sections.
Use `drawer` when the mobile menu needs to be a modal dialog: the sheet here does not trap focus.

teclado.acao: Move focus between the top-level items, wrapping around; with a panel open, the panel follows the item.
On an item with a panel, opens the panel and moves focus to the first link.
Inside the panel, move between links; `↑` on the first link closes the panel and returns focus to the item.
Inside the panel, go to the first or last link.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the item; with the mobile sheet open, closes the sheet and returns focus to the menu button.
On an item with a panel, open or close the panel; on the menu button, open or close the sheet.

acessibilidade: The top-level links sit in a `<nav>` named by `label` (“Main”); simple items receive `aria-current="page"`, but on an item with a panel the current state is only visual.
Panel triggers have `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, the panel is a `role="region"` with the item's name, and the outgoing face is `inert` during the switch.
The menu button has `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and a label that toggles; the sheet neither moves nor traps focus on open, and `Esc` closes it, returning focus to the button.
movimento: Past `scrollThreshold` (8 px), the background becomes opaque with a border and shadow and only lightens again near the top; the hover highlight (outside `centered`) and the current-section indicator slide between links.
The panel opens after 70 ms of mouse intent, the height follows the content on a spring that does not overshoot and, when moving to another item, the content enters from the side you moved toward.
The mobile sheet drops from the bar opening its height on a spring, with rows in sequence; with “reduce motion” on, panel and sheet only fade and the menu icon does not rotate.
responsivo: The header is its own container: below 760 px the links, the secondary action, and the panel disappear, the menu button appears, and widening again closes the sheet.
The sheet scrolls inside up to `--site-header-sheet-max` (default `100dvh - 65px`); set that variable when the header lives in a fixed-height container.
desempenho: Listens to `scroll` passively on the window or on `scrollContainer` and uses a `ResizeObserver` on the header; hover intent timers are cleared on unmount.
notasIA: Import the named component `SiteHeader`; the default export is `SiteHeaderBlock`, the preview with layout switching inside a scrolling page.
If the page scrolls inside an element, pass it as `scrollContainer`: it decides when the background becomes opaque and receives `overflow: hidden` while the mobile sheet is open.

Items with `links` only become a panel in `mega`; since the click event does not reach `onNavigate`, for client-side routing leave the destinations without `href` (they become buttons) and navigate in the callback.

quandoUsar: Strip of three or four highlight numbers on a landing or corporate page, each with a minimal chart that backs it up: trend, availability, distribution, or map.
When each number has a context line worth showing on demand, on hover or focus.
quandoEvitar: Use `metric-card` for a number with context in a dashboard; this strip is a page section and counts only once, when it enters the screen.
Use `animated-counter` when you only need a number that animates between values.
Use `bar-chart` or `line-chart` when the chart is the main content and the person needs to read values from it.

teclado.acao: Reaches each number that has `context`; with focus, the detail line gives way to the context line and the visual takes the accent color.

acessibilidade: Screen readers receive only the final value of each number, in hidden text; the animated count and the visuals are `aria-hidden`, so put in `detail` or `context` what the chart shows.
The strip is a `<section>` named by `title` (or “Key numbers”) and the numbers form a `<dl>`; `detail` and `context` both stay in the DOM, so both are read.
A number with `context` receives `tabIndex=0`, but the focus outline is removed: focus shows only through the line swap and the visual's color.
movimento: The first time 40% of the list enters the screen, the numbers rise in sequence (90 ms apart) and count from zero to the value in 1.6 s (`duration`); compact numbers count already in the final unit, from 0.0M to 2.3M.

When each number is almost at its value, the visual draws itself: line and map reveal from left to right, the bars grow in a wave and, in `divided`, the thin lines run across the strip and between the numbers.
With “reduce motion” on (read after hydration, with CSS covering the first paint), the numbers already appear at their final value and visuals and lines are ready, with no transition.
responsivo: The strip's container queries: up to 800 px the numbers go two by two and a strip of three stacks into one column; up to 520 px it goes one per row, with the visual beside the number.
The final width of each number is reserved from the start, so the count never pushes the layout.
desempenho: The count writes directly to the number's `textContent` on every frame, without re-rendering React, and `useInView` with `once` fires only once.
The `map` visual draws about 760 SVG circles, one per land point of the 80 × 30 grid, and is the heaviest of the four.
notasIA: Import the named component `StatsBand`; the default export is `StatsBandBlock`, the preview with layout switching, and `stats` uses the example data from `stats-band-data.ts`.

Each `Stat` takes `value`, `label` and, if you want, `prefix`, `suffix`, `decimals`, `notation: "compact"`, `detail`, `context`, and `visual` (`trend`, `uptime`, `distribution`, or `map`); the grid goes up to 4 columns.
`locale` is `en-US` by default so server and client format the same; use `pt-BR` for a decimal comma, and change the `key` to play the count again.

quandoUsar: Token swap with play money in demos, tutorials, or games: two fields with a token selector, a flip button, rate, and fees.
Standalone conversion card where the received amount is calculated instantly from the dollar prices you provide.
quandoEvitar: Use `money-input` for an amount field in one currency inside a regular form.
Use `prediction-market` to buy yes-or-no outcomes.
For real assets it does not work as is: there is no wallet or quote, network fee and slippage are constants, and a rejected swap returns to the start with no message.

teclado.acao: In the amount field, confirms the swap when the amount is greater than zero and fits the balance.
On the token selector, open the token menu (Radix).
In the menu, move between tokens; `Enter` or `Space` chooses, and choosing the token on the other side flips the pair.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the selector.

acessibilidade: Each field has a visible label and `aria-describedby` for the dollar value line, which turns into the insufficient-balance warning together with `aria-invalid`; the receive field is read-only and leaves the Tab order.
The selectors are Radix menus with radio items, each trigger states the side and the token in its `aria-label`, and the flip button states in its `aria-label` how the pair will end up.
On confirm, the form becomes `inert` and the receipt is `role="status"`, but focus is not moved to the receipt or restored to “New swap”; move it yourself if you need to.
movimento: On flip, the two fields swap places on a slightly bouncy spring, the one that goes up grows a little while the other sinks, and the arrow rotates 180°.
The rate line and the button label swap by sliding vertically; on confirm, the receipt covers the form on a spring, the circle appears, and the checkmark draws itself.
With “reduce motion” on, the fields swap instantly, the arrow does not rotate, labels only fade, the menu opens without animation, and the waiting indicator spins more slowly.
notasIA: Import the named component `TokenSwap`; the default export is the preview, and `sampleTokens` are invented tokens and prices, unrelated to real assets.

`onSwap(quote)` receives `pay`, `receive`, `amount`, and `received`: return a Promise to hold the pending state; balances only change in local state after success and each token's `balance` is only the initial one.

The rate comes from the dollar `price` values (the payer's price divided by the receiver's) and the fee from `feeRate` (default 0.3%); control the amount with `amount` and `onAmountChange` or use `defaultAmount`.

quandoUsar: Dashboard or financial product landing page that shows the card with balance and the latest transactions, with a button to hide the amounts.
When the back of the card (signature and security code) is part of the story and should open with a flip.
quandoEvitar: Use `tilt-card` when you only want the 3D tilt for other content, without a back, mask, or transactions.
Use `metric-card` to show a balance with context in a dashboard, without the card drawing.
Use `sortable-data-table` for long histories: the list here is short, with no pagination, filter, or sorting.

teclado.acao: On the “Show back” and “Hide amounts” buttons, flip the card or mask the amounts; the card itself does not receive focus.

acessibilidade: The face that is not showing is `aria-hidden` and `inert`; the number is read as “Card ending in” plus the four digits, and masked values as “Balance hidden”, in hidden text.
The two controls are buttons with `aria-pressed`; clicking the card is only a pointer shortcut on a `div` with no role, so the buttons are the accessible path.
Labels and hidden texts are hardcoded in English (“Show amounts”, “Recent activity”, “Card ending in”).
movimento: With a mouse, the card tilts up to 11° toward the pointer in 3D on a spring, under a glow that follows the pointer, and returns flat on leave.
The 180° flip uses a slightly bouncy spring; when masking, each digit turns into a dot one after another (16 ms apart) and the transactions rise in sequence on mount.
Touch does not tilt the card; with “reduce motion” on there is also no tilt, the flip is immediate, the digits swap without sliding, and the transactions appear all at once.
responsivo: The root is a container up to 23rem; the card keeps the payment-card proportion (1.586) and the balance scales with the width, from 1.5rem to 2rem (`8.6cqi`).
notasIA: Import the named component `WalletCard`; the default export is the preview with example data (holder, balance, and four transactions).
Control `masked` with `onMaskedChange` and `flipped` with `onFlippedChange` to store the choice; `transactions={[]}` hides the list and each `amount` is a signed number, negative for outflows.

Values are always formatted in `en-US` with the `currency` currency; the card only uses `last4`, and the `cvv` is printed on the back, protected only by the balance mask, so avoid passing the real code.
